changes: p3 name corrected from 'Śrīkṛṣṇa' to 'Kṛṣṇa': śrī is an honorific and is dropped.
p2 name changed to stem 'Kṛṣṇa', with bhaṭṭa kept as a title.

Relation p1→p2 changed from son_of to grandson_of. 'kṛṣṇabhaṭṭātmaja do bhasūnu' reads as 'son of [X]bhaṭṭa, who is the son of Kṛṣṇabhaṭṭa'. The garbled 'do bha' probably hides the father's name, perhaps (Mahā)devabhaṭṭa.
p1 confidence lowered to medium. The name may be a corruption of Divākara, and the genealogy is garbled.
Place of copying cleared. Rāmanagara is stated only as the owner's residence ('rāmanagara bālo' = 'of Rāmanagara'). It is kept in p3's residence field.
Era basis explained in notes. The colophon has a bare 'saṃvat'; it is taken as VS, so 1864 = 1807 CE (Caitra śukla 11, spring 1807).

notes: The commentary is the Vṛttaratnākarādarśa ('vṛttaratnākaraṃdarśaḥ'). The author's genealogy is corrupt: 'śrīmadbhārabdāvā(!)ṣṭha' = Bhāradvāja gotra? 'kṛṣṇabhaṭṭātmaja do bhasūnu' most likely means 'son of [?de]vabhaṭṭa, the son of Kṛṣṇabhaṭṭa'. The father's name is lost; it may be (Mahā)devabhaṭṭa, i.e. the Pāyaguṇḍe family (Bālakṛṣṇa → Mahādeva → Divākara/Dinakara), but this is unverified. 'samāptim aphāṇīt' is a corruption of 'agamat', and 'śrīmārṇastu' of 'śrīr astu'. The era is a bare 'saṃvat', taken as VS. 'rāmanagara bālo' (Hindi -vālā) marks Kṛṣṇa Jośī as being from Rāmanagara (possibly the one near Vārāṇasī). It is not explicitly the place of copying. The catalogue fields (scribe Padmanābhadvija; ŚS 1701 ≈ 1779 CE) do not match this colophon, which names no scribe and gives saṃvat 1864. These fields may belong to another colophon in the same MS or be a cataloguing error.
